title: String Compression II
summary: Given a string s and an integer k , remove at most k characters to minimize the length of the run-length encoded version of s .
statement: Given a string s and an integer k , remove at most k characters to minimize the length of the run-length encoded version of s . Run-length encoding involves replacing consecutive identical characters with the character followed by the count of repetitions, without adding '1' after single characters.
constraints: Delete at most k characters, then encode each equal-character run as the character plus its count when greater than one.
Return the minimum possible encoded length.
hints: Memoize the best result from a string index with a remaining deletion budget.
Choose the current character as the next run and scan forward, spending deletions on different characters.
Charge one character plus digits when the kept run reaches 2, 10, or 100; also consider deleting the current character.
Every optimal compressed string has a first kept run represented by one such scan.
editorial: Every optimal compressed string has a first kept run represented by one such scan.

tests.explanation: Deleting b and d produces aaaccc, encoded as a3c3 with length four.
Deleting both b characters joins four a characters into a4, of length two.
